chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

A man was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he recited this Verse: 'And those who hurt the believing men and the believing women without them being deserving of it, they are guilty indeed of a false accusation and a manifest sin.'
So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is the Reward for the one who causes the gladness to enter upon him?'
So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Ten good deeds.'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah, and a thousand, thousand (million) good deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for making a believer happy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elaborates on the spiritual weight of social interactions by contrasting the sin of causing distress to believers with the immense reward of bringing them joy. While the Quranic verse 33:58 highlights the 'manifest sin' of baseless hurt, the Imam quantifies the reciprocal virtue, promising ten million good deeds for those who alleviate a believer's sorrow. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* through emotional support and the high status of *furuj al-kurba* (relieving distress) in communal life.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘A man was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and he recited this Verse [33:58] And those who hurt the believing men and the believing women without them being deserving of it, they are guilty indeed of a false accusation and a manifest sin.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So what is the Reward for the one who causes the gladness to enter upon him?’
So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Ten good deeds’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and a thousand, thousand (million) good deeds’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa’dan ibn Muslim from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once a man, in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) recited this verse of the Holy Quran: ‘Those who annoy the believing men and women without reason will bear the sin for a false accusation, a manifest offense.’ [33:58]
The narrator has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then asked, ‘What then is the reward for sending joy to his heart?’
I said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, ten good deeds.’
The Imam said, ‘Yes, by Allah, it is one million good deeds.’”
